summary.text: The acid dissociation constant, Ka, describes how far an acid HA splits into its conjugate base A⁻ and a hydrogen ion H⁺ at equilibrium.
pKₐ is a logarithmic form of Ka, and a lower pKₐ means a stronger acid, while acetic acid has a pKₐ of 4.7.
With concentrations, pKₐ values let chemists predict a solution's pH, and they are needed to prepare buffer solutions.

facts.label: Pauling's rules
facts.value: One for polyprotic acids, one for oxyacids

items.prompt: At equilibrium, acid P is less dissociated than acid Q. Which statement is right?

options.label: Acid P has the lower Ka and is the weaker acid
Acid P has the higher Ka and is the stronger acid
Acid P has the lower Ka and is the stronger acid
The two acids must have the same Ka

items.explain: A lower Ka corresponds to a weaker acid, meaning one that is less dissociated at equilibrium.

items.prompt: Acid X has a pKₐ of 3 and acid Y has a pKₐ of 5. Which is the stronger acid?

options.label: Acid Y, because a higher pKₐ means a stronger acid
Acid X, because a lower pKₐ means a stronger acid
Acid X, because a lower pKₐ means a weaker acid
Neither, because pKₐ says nothing about strength

items.explain: A lower pKₐ corresponds to a stronger acid.

items.prompt: A reaction that absorbs heat is warmed up. What happens to the Ka of that dissociation?

options.label: It decreases
It stays the same, since Ka is fixed for an acid
It drops to zero
It increases

items.explain: For an endothermic reaction Ka increases and pKₐ decreases as temperature rises, which follows from Le Chatelier's principle.

items.prompt: When an acid HA dissociates in solution, which two species appear?

options.label: The conjugate base A⁻ and a hydrogen ion H⁺
A salt and some water
A metal and hydrogen gas
A hydroxide ion and the original acid

items.explain: The acid HA dissociates into its conjugate base A⁻ and a hydrogen ion H⁺.

items.prompt: A weak acid solution has sat until its concentrations stopped changing. What is going on at the molecular level?

options.label: All reactions have stopped completely
Only the forward reaction continues until the acid is gone
Forward and backward reactions both continue at the same rate
Only the backward reaction continues

items.explain: Equilibrium means the concentrations do not change over time because the forward and backward reactions occur at the same rate.

items.prompt: Many medicines are weak acids or bases. What can a drug's pKₐ help chemists estimate?

options.label: How cheaply a tablet can be made
How far the compound enters the bloodstream
How quickly a tablet crumbles on a shelf
How sweet the medicine tastes

items.explain: Knowing the pKₐ, together with the octanol-water partition coefficient, can be used to estimate the extent to which a compound enters the blood stream.
